facts.text: Every foot strike breaks a few red blood cells. It's one reason runners lose a little more iron than most.
For a few hours after a hard run, a hormone called hepcidin rises and your gut absorbs less iron.
HbA1c tracks your average blood sugar over roughly 2–3 months, because it rides on red blood cells that live about 120 days.
Many sports doctors look for ferritin above roughly 30–50 ng/mL in runners, higher than some lab cut-offs.
Low iron stores, even without anaemia, can show up as heavy legs and slower recovery.
B12 comes almost only from animal foods. Vegetarians, and people on long-term metformin or acid-reducing tablets, more often run low.
Endurance training expands plasma volume first, so haemoglobin can read a little low. Often that's harmless dilution.
Endurance training tends to raise HDL, the cholesterol that helps clear the rest.
TSH runs backwards: a high TSH usually means the thyroid is underactive, because the brain is signalling harder to get it going.
Runs over about 90 minutes in heat can drain sodium as well as water. Sweat can carry a lot of salt.
Low vitamin D is linked with more stress fractures in some studies of runners and military recruits.
A fasting test means 8–12 hours with only water. Even a sweet chai beforehand can skew fasting glucose.
Hard training the day before a test can raise CK, AST and even creatinine. Bloods read cleanest after a rest day.
Vitamin D is made in your skin from UVB light. Indoor days, covered skin and darker skin all cut how much you make, even in Indian sun.
Vitamin D, vitamin A and iron can build up in the body and cause harm at high doses. That's why D-Human reads before it recommends.
A supplement earns its place by fixing a measured gap. Without a test, it's a guess.
Ferritin is your iron savings account. It can run low long before haemoglobin drops, so a normal Hb doesn't rule out low iron.
A reference range is where most people in a lab's population fall. 'In range' isn't always 'ideal for you'.
One result is a snapshot. The same marker, same lab, same time of day, retested, shows you the trend.
Tea and coffee with meals can cut the iron you absorb from plant foods. Vitamin C in the same meal, like lemon on dal, helps.
